description: Table 1 is a single rendered data table (no plot, micrograph or spectrum), titled "Sample nomenclature of different processing conditions". It has three columns headed exactly "Sample condition", "Nomenclature for 3Al-0Si (M1)" and "Nomenclature for 3Al-1Si (M2)", and four data rows that map each processing step of both alloy chemistries to its acronym. Row 1 "As cast" gives M1-AC / M2-AC. Row 2 "Homogenized (1100 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching)" gives M1-HQ / M2-HQ. Row 3 "Hot rolled (~50 % thickness reduction at 1100-900 °C)" gives M1-HR / M2-HR. Row 4 "Inter-critical annealed (700 °C for 1 h followed by water quenching)" gives M1-IA / M2-IA. The table therefore fixes the naming convention used for the whole paper: M1 is the 3Al-0Si alloy and M2 the 3Al-1Si alloy, while the suffix encodes the processing state (AC = as cast, HQ = homogenized + quenched, HR = hot rolled, IA = inter-critical annealed). No property values are tabulated; the only quantities are the process parameters embedded in the condition text (1100 °C/2 h; ~50 % reduction at 1100-900 °C; 700 °C/1 h). All text is fully legible.

observations.observation: The table defines sample nomenclature for two alloy chemistries, labelled M1 (3Al-0Si) and M2 (3Al-1Si), across four processing conditions.
The three column headers read exactly "Sample condition", "Nomenclature for 3Al-0Si (M1)" and "Nomenclature for 3Al-1Si (M2)".
The as-cast condition is designated M1-AC for the 3Al-0Si alloy and M2-AC for the 3Al-1Si alloy.
The homogenized condition is defined as 1100 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching, with samples designated M1-HQ and M2-HQ.
The hot rolled condition is defined as ~50 % thickness reduction at 1100-900 °C, with samples designated M1-HR and M2-HR.
The inter-critical annealed condition is defined as 700 °C for 1 h followed by water quenching, with samples designated M1-IA and M2-IA.
The table contains no measured property values; only processing parameters and their acronyms are tabulated.
The caption states that the table gives the sample nomenclature of different processing conditions.
The citing text states that all these samples underwent standard metallographic preparation including grinding, coarse and fine polishing followed by chemical etching.
The citing text states that samples were etched using 2 % Nital solution (2 ml Nitric acid + 98 ml Ethanol) for 10-15 s to reveal the microstructure.
The citing text states that OM and SEM were used for microstructural imaging, EBSD for crystal orientation, and XRD (Cu-kα) for phase identification.
